Trigger record 2 at $9504 names this as its callback: $48BF jumps here with the record’s index, 1, in X when the view tile is column 7, row $0B. Store X at $9514, which is the opcode of the LDX #$FF there rather than its operand at $9515. Pass message $9517 (“DANGER! KEEP OUT”) to $77E0, then run the modified bytes at $9514.

Opcode byte of the LDX #$FF here, followed by RTS at $9516. $950A overwrites it with the trigger index before the message call. Only trigger record 2, index 1, names $950A, so the byte becomes $01 and the two bytes run as ORA ($FF,X). $77E0 returns with A=$20, the message’s control byte, and X=0, the length of its empty third line, so the instruction ORs A with the byte that the zero-page pointer at $FF/$00 addresses, and the routine returns without restoring X. The record’s count of 1 lets it run once per load, and $4A43, the main loop’s next call at $0437, reads neither A nor X.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “” / “DANGER! KEEP OUT” / “”, then the control byte $20. The instruction sequence at $950D loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 32 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.
